title: Punctual purity of monomial hypersurfaces over a trait
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

A trait is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ a Noetherian local domain of dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal; a uniformizer $\pi$ is a generator of that maximal ideal.

Let $\ell$ be invertible in $R$, fix a uniformizer $\pi$, let $n\geq1$, and let $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ be nonnegative integers not all zero. Then the Noetherian scheme
$$T=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(T_1^{e_1}\cdots T_n^{e_n}-\pi)\bigr)$$
is regular and punctually pure. The assertion allows zero exponents and exponents divisible by $\ell$ or by the positive residue characteristic; no completeness, henselianity, or excellence of $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definition 3.5.11 and Proposition 3.5.12 with proof and Lemma 3.5.13(i)--(vi), printed pp.250--251; section 3.5 begins on printed p.248 with an arbitrary trait.

proof.text: First prove regularity without asserting generic smoothness over the original trait. The ring $R$ is a DVR by [lem-sc-principal-ideal-dvr]. Let $g$ be the gcd of the nonzero exponents and put $b_i=e_i/g$. By [lem-sbc-dvr-uniformizer-root-algebra], $R_g=R[u]/(u^g-\pi)$ is a trait with uniformizer $u$. There is an explicit ring isomorphism $R_g[T_i]/(\prod T_i^{b_i}-u)\simeq R[T_i]/(\prod T_i^{e_i}-\pi)$: send $u$ to $\prod T_i^{b_i}$ and each $T_i$ to itself, with inverse induced by the same variables. Since the nonzero $b_i$ have gcd one, at least one is nonzero in the fraction field of $R_g$ (in characteristic $p>0$, they cannot all be divisible by $p$). Thus [lem-per-primitive-monomial-trait-geometry] proves that this scheme, hence $T$, is Noetherian, integral and regular. This works for every tuple in the statement.

It remains to prove punctual purity. Delete the $r$ zero exponents, leaving a nonempty positive tuple $a$. The original coordinate ring is exactly the polynomial ring in the deleted variables over the coordinate ring of $V(S,\pi,a)$. The maps in both directions are the identity on all remaining variables and coefficients. Hence $T\simeq\mathbf A^r_{V(S,\pi,a)}$. Its projection is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. Once purity has been proved for the positive tuple, [lem-per-smooth-punctual-purity-ascent] proves it for $T$: both models are regular by Step 1 and of finite type over the given trait. Hence all remaining steps treat positive exponents.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.12 proof, p.251, removal of zero exponents by Corollary 3.5.6.

proof.text: For the all-one tuple the coordinate-divisor Kummer maps are isomorphisms by [lem-per-semistable-coordinate-divisor-purity]; [lem-per-monomial-boundary-purity-criterion] therefore proves punctual purity. This applies over every auxiliary trait as well. For an integer $d>0$ use the trait $R_d=R[u]/(u^d-\pi)$ from [lem-sbc-dvr-uniformizer-root-algebra]. Eliminating $u$ gives $R_d[T_i]/(\prod T_i-u)\simeq R[T_i]/(\prod T_i^d-\pi)$, explicitly $u\mapsto\prod T_i$, $T_i\mapsto T_i$, with inverse on variables. Thus the equal-exponent model $V(S,\pi,d,\ldots,d)$ is punctually pure for every positive $d$, even if $d$ is divisible by the residue characteristic or by $\ell$. The coefficient prime remains invertible in the auxiliary trait.

Suppose now that the positive exponents $a_i$ are all prime to $\ell$. Put $d=\operatorname{lcm}(a_i)$ and $q_i=d/a_i$. Map $Y=V(S,\pi,d,\ldots,d)$ to $X=V(S,\pi,a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ by $T_i\mapsto U_i^{q_i}$. Over the coordinate ring $B$ of $X$, its algebra is $B[U_1,\ldots,U_n]/(U_i^{q_i}-T_i)_i$: eliminating the $T_i$ gives exactly $Y$. Successive division by these monic polynomials gives a basis $\prod U_i^{j_i}$, $0\le j_i<q_i$. Consequently this is a finite presentation with a finite free module of rank $N=\prod q_i>0$; it is flat by [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat], and has constant fibre degree $N$ by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Since $\ell\nmid d$, also $\ell\nmid N$. For each coordinate divisor $H_i$ of $X$, its inverse image is $U_i^{q_i}=0$, and its reduction is the coordinate divisor $U_i=0$ of $Y$, since that quotient is a polynomial ring over the residue field. The boundary criterion supplies regularity of these divisors and purity of their pairs in $Y$ by Step 3. Apply [lem-per-finite-flat-regular-divisor-purity-descent] to each pair and then [lem-per-monomial-boundary-purity-criterion] to $X$. This proves punctual purity of $X$. No generic-etaleness assumption is used.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.13(v) and its proof, p.251; Proposition 3.4.3, p.246.

proof.text: For a positive tuple $a$, compare $X=V(S,\pi,a_1,a_2,\ldots)$ and $X'=V(S,\pi,\ell a_1,a_2,\ldots)$ by $T_1=U_1^\ell$, keeping the other coordinates. The second algebra is exactly $B[U_1]/(U_1^\ell-T_1)$, where $B$ is the first algebra. The coordinate divisor $D=(T_1=0)$ and its root divisor $D'=(U_1=0)$ are regular effective Cartier divisors by the boundary criterion, and both have coordinate ring $\kappa(s)[T_2,\ldots,T_n]$. They are punctually pure by [lem-per-prime-field-punctual-purity]: the residue field, hence this regular scheme, is an algebra over its prime field. The root lemma [lem-per-kummer-root-regular-divisor-purity] identifies purity of the two pairs. Since both divisors are punctually pure, [lem-per-punctual-purity-two-of-three] says that purity at all points of $D$ is equivalent to purity of the first pair, and similarly for $D'$ and the second pair. Thus purity along the whole first divisor is equivalent to purity along the whole second divisor. Off these divisors the same root lemma gives a surjective etale cover, so [lem-per-punctual-purity-etale-locality] identifies punctual purity everywhere on those complements. The closed divisors and their complements exhaust the schemes; hence $X$ is punctually pure if and only if $X'$ is. Permuting the variables gives this equivalence for multiplication of any one positive exponent by $\ell$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.13(vi) and its proof, p.251; Proposition 3.4.5, pp.246--248.

proof.text: For the original positive tuple write $a_i=\ell^{v_i}b_i$, where $v_i\ge0$, $b_i>0$ and $\ell\nmid b_i$. Apply the equivalence established in Step 5 to divide one exponent by $\ell$ whenever its $v_i$ is positive. Induct on the nonnegative integer $\sum_i v_i$: division decreases it by one and the base tuple has every exponent prime to $\ell$. Step 4 proves purity for that base tuple, so the equivalences prove it for the original positive tuple. Step 2 restores all zero exponents; regularity and Noetherianity were proved in Step 1. Thus every clause of the statement holds without any excellence, completeness or henselianity assumption.

source.place: Final paragraph of Proposition 3.5.12 proof, p.251.

proof_origin.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.5.12 and Lemma 3.5.13, pp.250--251; Corollary 3.5.6; Propositions 3.4.3 and 3.4.5.

The item statement is unchanged and matches 3.5.12. Step 1: g = gcd of the nonzero exponents, auxiliary trait R_g = R[u]/(u^g - pi); I checked the isomorphism on generators. gcd(b) = 1, so the primitive node applies; this fixes the inseparable (p) case in characteristic p. Step 2: zero exponents give A^r over V(a); smoothness from the Lean-closed sbc node, then the ascent node (3.5.6), whose finite-type and regular hypotheses hold. Step 3: semistable node plus the boundary criterion give V(1,...,1), and the root trait R_d gives V(d,...,d). Step 4: the map T_i -> U_i^{q_i} is finite free with a monomial basis of rank prod q_i, prime to ell; the reduced preimage of H_i is V(U_i); descent (3.4.3) and the criterion finish. Step 5: Kummer root (3.4.5) with f = T_1, prime-field purity of D and D' (both kappa(s)[T_2..]), two-of-three along D, and pointwise etale locality on the surjective etale complement cover; this is more careful than the source. Step 6: the induction on the sum of ell-valuations is properly set up. All six new nodes are true and match their source places: the primitive node (Eisenstein domain, pi not in m^2, Jacobian check), 3.4.3, 3.4.5 (V(U) = reduced preimage, extra clauses true), 3.5.6, 3.5.13(iv) (special fibre inside the union of the H_i, generic fibre pure by prime-field purity), and the semistable pair form, equivalent via the criterion to the Illusie 2004 / Rapoport-Zink input. They are statement-only and self-contained, cited ids exist, blueprint.from and via are set, and all three search kinds are recorded. No duplicates in the DAG (existing nodes cover 3.2.3, 3.2.5, 3.5.5, 3.5.7 and etale locality only), no restated clause, no cycle, no SGA. I accept the declared tool uses: principal-ideal DVR, root algebra, the finite-free flatness Mathlib leaf, and the Lean-closed affine-space smoothness. Batch-5 flags: all three cited nodes reach only generic sec-trace-formula/pod infrastructure, namely the D+ adjunction for an exact left adjoint, the closed-immersion strict-localisation fibre product, and site, topos and projective-bundle geometry. None is part of the trace formula or Poincare duality. regular-immersion-class-calculus only defines the Kummer class and was already a stmt_dep of the item. All accepted. Advisory for the maintainer: Illusie 2004 and Rapoport-Zink are not in literature/; the later split of lem-per-semistable-coordinate-divisor-purity will need them as WANTED. The primitive node lists krull-dimension in stmt_deps without a bracket citation (it is used implicitly by 'dimension one').
